Subject: SIG follow-up: data handling Qs

Marcus — thanks for the SIG PDF you sent last week. Our security team had a few follow-ups specifically around the items marked in the data handling section: retention of prompt/request logs, whether customer content is ever used to train models, and how a customer can opt out of training. Can you provide concise answers and any artifacts (SLA language, configuration screens, or runbooks) we can attach to our procurement packet?

High-level items we need:
- How long are request/prompt logs retained by default? Are there short/long retention tiers?
- Are prompts, responses, or derived embeddings ever used for model training or offline evals? If so, under what conditions?
- What is the opt-out mechanism for training on customer data? Is it self-serve or via contract addendum?
- Evidence: an export of the retention policy, a screenshot of the console toggle (if applicable), and any legal language we can reference.

We are aiming to finish our vendor review by next Wed (3/31). Appreciate anything you can share quickly.

—Ellen

Velora Therapeutics

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (Security) and Priya (Legal) to ensure technical + contractual accuracy. Summary answers below; I attached a working PDF with the SIG answers and our current retention SLA for quick reference (SIG_answers_v1.pdf, Data_Retention_SLA.pdf).

Short answers (high level):
- Retention: Request logs (api request/response metadata) are retained 30 days by default. Customers can elect a 0-day retention (no request bodies stored) or a longer retention tier (90/365 days) under Dedicated/Private plans. See Data_Retention_SLA.pdf for contractual tiers.
- Training: We do not use customer prompts or responses to train or improve public/shared models by default. For Hosted customers, data is used for service reliability (e.g., debugging) for a short window, unless customer explicitly opts into model-improvement programs. Any training-on-customer-data program is opt-in and governed by a separate addendum.
- Opt-out: Training opt-out is implemented as a settings flag on the account (self-service for Hosted accounts) or by contract for Dedicated/Private with an explicit clause. For customers that need immediate confirmation, our Support team can apply an account-level opt-out within 24 hours and provide written confirmation.

Neha/Priya — can you confirm the technical details for KV cache behavior and KMS usage? I left a placeholder in the attachment for the screenshot of the console toggle; we can produce a redacted screenshot if needed.

Next steps:
1) Neha to add the technical playbook and opt-out steps.
2) Priya to prepare suggested contract language (if Velora prefers an addendum).
3) I’ll share DocuSign link if you want an addendum signed.

Thanks — Marcus

Hi Ellen — Neha from Redwood Security here, thanks for the follow-ups. Quick technical bullets:

1) Request bodies: by default our hosted offering persists the full request/response body (prompts + outputs) for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. Customers can configure:
   - "0-day" retention (no request/response bodies stored) — stores only minimal metadata for billing
   - 30-day default
   - 90 / 365 day tiers for customers on Reserved Capacity or with business need (contracted)
   - In Dedicated and Private deployments the default is governed by the customer's configuration and contract (most enterprise customers choose 0-day or 30-day).

   Note: embeddings derived from prompts are treated the same as request/response data unless explicitly redacted by the customer.

2) Training opt-in/out:
   - Training with customer data is strictly opt-in. When a customer opts in, we log consent and the date range of data covered. If a customer later elects to opt out, we stop including new data in training going forward. Retroactive removal of data from models is addressed on a case-by-case basis (we offer data deletion from staging/training datasets where feasible; production model weights removal is not guaranteed unless covered by a custom agreement). We document this behavior in the Training Opt-Out Playbook (attached).

3) KMS / encryption:
   - Hosted: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via integrations with major cloud KMS providers for encryption-at-rest of persisted logs and backups — this is available on an opt-in basis for Hosted customers and included by default on Dedicated/Private. Keys are used for storage encryption; request processing in-memory still uses ephemeral keys managed by the runtime.

Artifacts included: training_optout_playbook.md (procedural steps + sample support ticket language), KMS_integration_overview.pdf (architecture diagram). I can also generate a redacted console screenshot showing the retention toggle if you want for procurement.

If Velora needs contract language, Priya has draft wording that maps to our standard addendum (Priya — assigning to you).

Best,
Neha Kapoor
